evidence.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.
The change from parent to daughter happens at a constant rate, called the half-life.
A radioactive isotope (the parent) of one chemical element naturally converts to a stable isotope (the daughter)
Now we can use minerals that contain naturally occurring radioactive elements to calculate the numeric age of a rock in years.

objectives: Explain half-life as the time for one-half of parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms
Describe how measurements of remaining parent and produced daughter atoms are used to compute rock age
